And I think we also want to bring awareness to the Lyme disease that they can carry and how careful we need to be. So whereas Lyme disease is the most commonly reported tick-borne disease in the United States, accounting for over 80% of all tick-borne illness. And whereas Lyme disease is spread to people by the bite of an infected tick. Immature ticks become infected by feeding on small infected mammals such as white-footed mice. Once infected, the tick can then spread the disease to humans through its bites. And Lyme disease is not spread person to person. And whereas approximately 476,000 people in the United States are diagnosed with and treated annually for Lyme disease in the US, including approximately 4,000 in New Jersey alone. Yet it is known that Lyme disease is an underreported illness. And therefore the actual number of people with Lyme disease in New Jersey is likely much higher. And whereas Lyme disease is a complex, multi-system illness caused by bacteria which if caught early can be treated easily with antibiotics, but if left untreated can invade the nervous system, brain, heart, and multiple organs of the body, causing years of pain, suffering, severe disability, and even death. And whereas ticks that carry Lyme disease can carry several other pathogens and occasional co-infections have been reported. And whereas while the risk of contracting a tick-borne illness can be year round, the nymphal ticks, which are the size of a poppy seed are most active in the spring and summer months. And whereas people can reduce their risk of contracting Lyme disease by avoiding wooded areas with dense shrubs and leaf litter where ticks like to hide, making their yards less attractive to ticks by keeping their lawns mowed, using safe and effective repellent on themselves and their pets to keep ticks from attaching to skin and frequently checking themselves and especially children when in common tick-infested areas. And whereas if a tick is found attached to their skin, people should remove it as soon as possible and disinfect the bite area. Proper removal of a tick within 48 hours of being bitten can reduce the risk of infection. And whereas people need to be aware of the early symptoms of Lyme disease, a rash that looks like a bullseye, tiredness, fever, headache, stiff neck, muscle aches, joint pain, because when treated early, antibiotic therapy for three to four weeks is generally effective. And whereas to avoid the potentially serious long-term serious health effects, it is essential to educate the community about preventative steps to avoid contracting Lyme disease as well as the effectiveness of early treatment for certainly contracted disease. Now, therefore be it proclaimed that I, Mayor Shelley Brindle, do hereby proclaim May 2021 as Lyme Disease Awareness Month in the town of Westfield. And in doing so, I encourage all community members to take advantage of the comprehensive resources available from the New Jersey Department of Health and from Lymedisease.org, one of the oldest Lyme disease advocacy organizations in the country to help spread Lyme disease awareness and prevention education. So thank you for bringing this to our attention. I know I'm not alone when I say I know more than one person that has suffered from Lyme disease, much more serious than others. So please be aware. And whereas on December 11th, 2021, USFCA issued its first emergency use authorization for COVID-19 vaccine. And on December 14th, 2020, the New Jersey Department of Health implemented comprehensive vaccine education and prioritization plan. And whereas initially in order to receive the vaccine, appointments at designated vaccination sites were required. And because demand was so high, they were very difficult to secure. And whereas in early February of 2021, a vulnerable populations work group was formed to engage community members and helping to identify vulnerable persons who may need assistance for obtaining COVID-19 vaccination and to provide education to those who may have questions about the vaccine. And whereas meetings were held in February and March to identify the areas to focus on, to encourage and assist with vaccination registration. And whereas two education webinars, one sponsored by Lifelong Westfield and one by the Westfield Regional Board of Health were held to advise and answer questions about vaccine development, hesitancy, side effects, and the importance of vaccination to help protect those most vulnerable to COVID-19. And whereas a drive-by registration effort was coordinated by the Westfield Neighborhood Council, which registered several residents who were then able to receive the COVID-19 vaccination. And whereas in working with our county partners, the vulnerable populations work group was able to hold a COVID-19 vaccination pop-up site on March 26th, 2021 in the community room of the Westfield Municipal Building. In order to do so, members of the group worked tirelessly within a short 48 hour timeframe to identify our African-American, Hispanic, senior, and handicapped neighbors who may have wanted the vaccine, but were unable to secure an appointment. The group's outreach was very successful. Approximately 200 persons using all of the shots they had that day were vaccinated at the pop-up clinic. speaker: markp
text: Just, I'm sorry to interrupt, and believe me, I'm the first to vote for the motion to adjourn. But I did want to just, if we have just a few minutes just to give a quick update on the Cannabis Commission and the meeting, the public meeting that we have coming up this Thursday, just to give everyone kind of a summary of what the meeting's about, what the commission's considering. Ultimately, it's a decision whether to opt in or opt out. And the basic decision is under the law, towns have 180 days, and that's until August 21st of 2021 to either prohibit outright or limit the number of establishments, distributors, and delivery services of the location, manner, and times of operation and establish civil penalties for violations of certain ordinances. And as we set forth in the website, once a municipality opts in, that decision remains in effect for five years. And if a municipality opts out, Westfield opts out, we can always thereafter opt in at any time. There's no limitation. And it's not just limited to retail operations. There's six different classes of licenses that the state is issuing, a cultivator's license, manufacturer, wholesale, distributor, retail, and delivery. So there's a variety of different things to consider. So in addition to me and Councilman Dardia, the commission's composed of 14 additional people, residents and town employees. And of those 14, excluding me and Dardia, only one is elected and all of them have volunteered to take their time to make a thoughtful and a considered recommendation to the council. And importantly, part of the commission's goal, we've met a few times already, and the part of the goal is to incorporate public input into the recommendations. And we feel it's really important to hear from residents. And we recognize the conflict between one thing, the responses to the master plan questionnaire, where in 2018, a majority of the residents or respondents preferred no cannabis retailers within the town. And you contrast that with Westfield's support in favor of legalizing cannabis in November of 2020, which at 69% was actually two points exceeding the state average in favor of the legalization, which was roughly around 67%. So we're trying to go about this two different ways. This coming Thursday, we've got a public input meeting. The commission's gonna host a public input meeting via Zoom beginning at seven o'clock. The meeting will also be streamed via Facebook Live, but all those who wish to speak have to join via Zoom. And if you go to the main town webpage and search cannabis, it's easy to find the link. And then we're also accepting emails. So for those who can't attend on Thursday, comments may also be submitted via email through May 20th. And the email address is cannabiscomments, that's one word, at westfieldnj.gov. And the email address will be open basically for almost a full two weeks, which should give everyone in town a chance to share their opinion. And I can say that we've already had several responses so far. And the other thing I do wanna point out is what the meeting's not about. Importantly, there's no current proposal for permitting a dispensary downtown or anywhere else in Westfield. The whole concept, and the only thing that we're considering right now is whether or not to opt in or opt out generally. The meeting's not about the appropriateness of legalizing cannabis in the first place, or they already passed law on the statewide level. And it's also not about keeping cannabis out of Westfield. One thing that's important that I think residents need to know is that the state law does not permit municipalities to restrict or prohibit delivery services. And so irrespective of the town's decision to opt in or opt out, delivery must be permitted within Westfield under state law. And also I point out that one of our closest neighbors, Scotch Plains, among some others, have already opted in both on Route 22 and then also on Plainfield Avenue, a section of Plainfield Avenue. So I look forward to hearing everybody's comments. Hopefully most of the, or all of the commission's gonna be able to be there to listen to it. And we're also looking forward to reviewing the comments that come in.
